ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: $Cu^{2+}$ ions appear blue in solution, and the $NO_3^-$ ion is colorless. The absorbance of a $Cu(NO_3)_2$ solution is measured at various wavelengths using a spectrophotometer. To determine the concentration of a $Cu(NO_3)_2$ solution of unknown concentration, what wavelength of light would produce the best results?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a curve of absorbance changing with wavelength; the vertical axis is labeled Absorbance, and the horizontal axis is labeled Wavelength (nm). The horizontal axis ticks include about 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800 nm. The curve has a smaller peak near the shorter wavelength of about 250–300 nm, and drops to a trough near about 450 nm; afterward the curve rises rapidly and reaches the highest peak between 600–700 nm, with the peak top located at about 640 nm. Reasoning: When using spectrophotometry to determine an unknown concentration, the maximum absorption wavelength should be selected, because the absorbance change there is most sensitive to concentration, and the measurement result is best. The maximum absorption peak in the figure is at about 640 nm, so light of 640 nm should be selected.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image graph: absorbance is plotted on the vertical axis and wavelength in nm on the horizontal axis. Locate the wavelength where the absorbance curve reaches its highest point; this is around 640 nm. Apply the rule that an unknown concentration should be measured at the wavelength of maximum absorbance. Therefore select 640 nm.
